cause: save()/start() deleted control keys (numFiles, timeout) from the writer's own options dict to keep them out of pandas kwargs, consuming them on first use; freq existed only after trigger()
evidence_loop: pytest tests/test_5_files_write_batch.py tests/test_5_files_write_stream.py: assert 2 == 4 (16), KeyError 'timeout' (14) -> green
expected: options are read, never consumed: every save honours numFiles; timeout defaults to 20 s and trigger has a default
solution: pop the control keys from a per-call copy passed to the file handler; freq defaults to 1 s in __init__ (documented)

cause: size had two owners: FileWriter kept its own _size=1000 and DataGenerator resolved its size by copied ternaries in get_df and stream_dict; the writer closures (built in __init__) never read the generator size
evidence_loop: pytest tests/test_5_files_write_batch.py tests/test_5_files_write_stream.py tests/test_2_data_generator_fails.py on pre-fix prod: 20 failed (assert 1000 == 5 x16, assert 1000 == 7, AttributeError _size, DID NOT RAISE RandEngineError x2) -> green
expected: 5000 rows (int or callable size): the writer uses the generator size unless .write.size() overrides it
solution: operator ruling 2026-10-03: delete .write.size(); DataGenerator owns size alone via _resolve_size() (int or callable, re-read per file/microbatch, RandEngineError naming .size(n) when unset) used by get_df, stream_dict and both writer closures; writers resolve every microbatch before any overwrite deletion
symptom: DataGenerator(spec).size(5000).write.format('csv').save(path) writes 1000 rows; FileWriter keeps its own _size=1000 and the generator size never flows to it (README writing example)
title: DataGenerator.size() never reaches .write/.writeStream: files always hold 1000 rows

expected: Every value lies within [min, max] as given.

expected: Both engines treat integers max identically (inclusive, as the pandas engine does).
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c 'from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, functions as F; from rand_engine.main.spark_generator import SparkGenerator; s=SparkSession.builder.master("local[1]").getOrCreate(); print(sorted(r[0] for r in SparkGenerator(s,F,{"a":{"method":"integers","kwargs":{"min":0,"max":1}}}).size(20000).get_df().select("a").distinct().collect()))' -> [0]
symptom: SparkCore.gen_ints casts rand()*(max-min)+min, so max is exclusive; NPCore uses randint(min, max+1), inclusive. min=0 max=1 on Spark yields only 0.
title: Spark integers never reaches max while pandas includes it

cause: DataGenerator.__init__ stored one FileBatchWriter/FileStreamWriter per generator (self.write/self.writeStream); every .write chain mutated that one object, so format/mode/options leaked into later chains
evidence_loop: pytest tests/test_5_files_write_batch.py tests/test_5_files_write_stream.py: before fix 17 failed (16 test_writing_single_file, 1 test_stream_defaults_timeout_20s_trigger_1s), after 77 passed; full suite 502 passed
expected: Each access to .write/.writeStream returns a fresh writer with defaults (Spark DataFrameWriter semantics).
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c 'from rand_engine import DataGenerator as G; from rand_engine.examples import CommonRandSpecs as C; import os; g=G(C.customers()).size(10); g.write.format("parquet").option("numFiles",2); g.write.save("/tmp/x/c"); print(os.listdir("/tmp/x/c"))' -> 2 part_*.parquet files
solution: Deleted the stored writers and _writer/_stream_writer; write/writeStream are properties returning a new writer per access (Spark DataFrameWriter semantics). Per-call options copy in save()/start() kept: a single reused writer object still needs it (test_writing_multiple_files_append).
symptom: DataGenerator.__init__ builds self.write/self.writeStream once (data_generator.py:26-27); format/options set on one chain persist into the next: after g.write.format('parquet').option('numFiles',2), a bare g.write.save(c) writes 2 parquet files.
title: g.write/g.writeStream are one object per generator; settings leak across chains

cause: FileBatchWriter.save called the size-resolving microbatch closure once per file, so each of numFiles files got the full generator size (size x numFiles rows).
evidence_diff: net-negative: prod +10/-12, tests +15/-6 (tests include reviewer F1 fold: dedicated abandoned-chain test, matrix restored)
evidence_loop: pytest tests/test_5_files_write_batch.py: 16 failed (StopIteration: callable size read per file) before; 50 passed after; repro size(10)+numFiles 2 -> 2 files, 10 rows
expected: size rows total, split across numFiles files.
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c 'from rand_engine import DataGenerator as G; from rand_engine.examples import CommonRandSpecs as C; import os,pandas as pd; G(C.customers()).size(10).write.format("csv").option("numFiles",2).save("/tmp/x/n"); print(sum(len(pd.read_csv("/tmp/x/n/"+f)) for f in os.listdir("/tmp/x/n")))' -> 20
solution: FileWriter takes (size_def, microbatch_def(size)) for both writers: size_def = DataGenerator._resolve_size, microbatch_def = wrapped_df_generator. Batch save() resolves size once and divmod-splits it across files in file order (counts differ by <=1, sum = size); stream resolves once per tick (unchanged).
symptom: FileBatchWriter generates the full generator size per file, so size(10) with numFiles=2 writes 20 rows; docs/3_WRITING_FILES.md:461 promises size(50_000)+numFiles=10 gives '~5000 rows each'.
title: numFiles multiplies rows instead of splitting size across files
